name: Question 12
problem:
Solve the following congruence

$$
5x+3≡22\,(\text{mod}\,12),
$$

expressing your answer as a nonnegative integer smaller than $12.$

*Hint: You may wish to use trial and error to find the appropriate multiplicative inverse.*

$x≡$
{{field-1}}$\,(\text{mod}\,12)$
worked_solution:
First, we reduce our congruence to a congruence of the form $ax≡b,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x+3 & ≡22\, & (\text{mod}\,12) \\ 5x+3-3 & ≡22-3\, & (\text{mod}\,12) \\ 5x & ≡19\, & (\text{mod}\,12) \\ 5x & ≡1\cdot 12+7\, & (\text{mod}\,12) \\ 5x & ≡7\, & (\text{mod}\,12)\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that a linear congruence $ax≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n)$ has a unique solution modulo $n$ if and only if $\text{gcd}(a,n)=1.$

In the given congruence, we have $a=5$ and $n=12$, and

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(5,12)=1.
$$

So, our congruence does indeed have a unique solution.

To find the solution, we need to multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of $5\,(\text{mod}\,12).$ To find the inverse of $5\,(\text{mod}\,12)$, we compute the exponents of $5\,(\text{mod}\,12)$ until we get a result of $1\,(\text{mod}\,12):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{2} & ≡25≡2\cdot 12+1≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,12)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $5\cdot 5≡1\,(\text{mod}\,12),$ which means that $5$ is the multiplicative inverse of $5$ (modulo $12$).

Now, multiplying both sides of our congruence by $5,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x & ≡7 &  & (\text{mod}\,12) \\ 5\cdot 5x & ≡5\cdot 7 &  & (\text{mod}\,12) \\ (5\cdot 5)x & ≡35 &  & (\text{mod}\,12) \\ 1\cdot x & ≡11+2\cdot 12 &  & (\text{mod}\,12) \\ x & ≡11 &  & (\text{mod}\,12)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x≡11\,(\text{mod}\,12).$
